title: [FR] Support uv package installer when inferring requirements (i.e. when logging model)
body:
### Willingness to contribute

No. I cannot contribute this feature at this time.

### Proposal Summary

When using the **[uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)** package manager to create virtual environments and install packages mlflow is unable to infer requirements.txt when auto-logging a model.

I guess this is caused by uv behaviour being slightly different to pip.

### Motivation

> #### What is the use case for this feature?
ability to auto-log models (with inferred dependencies) based on environments managed by the uv package manager

> #### Why is this use case valuable to support for MLflow users in general?
usage of uv is increasing. It's faster than pip.

> #### Why is this use case valuable to support for your project(s) or organization?

> #### Why is it currently difficult to achieve this use case?
errors encountered unless we manually log the model with explicitly specified dependencies in the argument.

### Details

_No response_

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
+1 for this!

A potential route might to have `mlflow.models.infer_pip_requirements()` detect the presence of a `uv.lock` file. If present, it can determine the pip requirements by using a subprocess that runs `uv export --no-dev --no-hashes --no-editable --frozen --locked`

Likewise, `mlflow.sklearn.get_default_conda_env()` could create a conda file by looking for the presence of a `.python-version` file (which `uv` will add to projects)

comments.body:
We started exploring this. Do you want to log `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` files with the model, and use them to restore the environment via `uv sync`?

For example, let's say you manage everything with uv. You only have `pyproejct.toml` and `uv.lock`, no `requirements.txt`. Do you want to log them with the model?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I'm not sure how it works exactly, but things like databricks serving endpoints seems to build the environment from the conda specification.

The way we work now is to export the uv.lock file to a requirements.txt file (`uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-header --no-editable --no-hashes --output-file {requirements_file}`), read that in, and log it to mlflow. Something like this:

```python
conda_env = {
    "name": "mlflow-env",
    "channels": ["conda-forge"],
    "dependencies": [f"python={python_version}", {"pip": requirements}],
}
mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(
    conda_env=conda_env,
    ...
)
```

So having a `uv.lock` file logged with the model is a nice-to-have. In the future mlflow might want to use `uv` to create environments, and then it's a must-have. Might as well start including it now already.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
project_root parameter makes a lot of sense, good abstraction because it can be extended to any python environment system. But it does make it harder to test, as you'll have to create temporary directories with the required files. 

Maybe instead of `conda_env` and `pip_requirements` we could use `python_version` and `requirements: path | list[str]`. Then you can pass a uv.lock file, a requirements.txt file, or a list with requirements.

Btw, it's worth the time to read the docs for `uv` start to finish. The concepts look very familiar to older tools like `rye` and `poetry`.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
@participant4 Thanks. Nothing fancy, I simply use it as a dependency manager. 

* `uv add` installs a dependency, but also automatically registers it in the `pyproject.toml` file: no more forgetting to manually declare dependencies in vanilla `pip`
* `uv remove` to remove dependencies, also from `pyproject.toml` file: no unnecessary dependencies when rebuilding the environment
* `uv` registers the python version in `.python-version`: not supported in vanilla `pip`
* `uv` is _fast_: 
  * nice when packaging solutions in Docker images, which will be built much faster 
  * especially nice because Docker image building typically happens in CI/CD pipelines, where each second spent in a CI/CD pipeline costs money
  * reduces 'startup' time during serverless model serving, where the entire environment needs to be set up

Hope this helps!

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
@participant4, I think @participant5' comment is excellent, but I’d like to expand on it with a practical example. Let’s compare creating a new package using `uv` and a "standard" toolchain.

Start by initializing the package:

```shell
$ uv init --package mypackage
$ cd mypackage
```

Now, the project structure includes:

```plaintext
.gitignore
.python-version
README.md
pyproject.toml
src/mypackage/__init__.py
```

For example, `pyproject.toml` contains:

```toml
[project]
name = "mypackage"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
authors = [{ name = "Your Name", email = "<email-scrubbed>" }]
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = []

[project.scripts]
mypackage = "mypackage:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
```

You can already run the package (note that the `mypackage` executable is defined in `[project.scripts]`):

```shell
$ uv run mypackage
Hello from mypackage!
```

#### Environments

Running any `uv run` command automatically creates and manages a virtual environment in `.venv`. Common commands:

- `uv run python`: Use the correct interpreter.
- `uv run python src/file.py`: Execute scripts using the project environment.
- `uv run pytest`: Run tests with `pytest`.

To clean up, delete `.venv` — `uv` will recreate it reproducibly with `uv sync` or another `uv run`.

#### Adding Dependencies

Add runtime or development dependencies easily:

```shell
$ uv add numpy pandas
$ uv add --dev mypy
```

This updates `pyproject.toml` and generates a `uv.lock` file, ensuring reproducibility:

```toml
dependencies = ["numpy>=1.24.0", "pandas>=1.5.0"]
[dependency-groups]
dev = ["mypy>=1.0.0"]
```

#### Building and Publishing

Building packages is straightforward (while `uv run` will install all dependencies, `uv build` will ignore dev-dependencies):

```shell
$ uv build
```

Publishing to a registry is equally simple:

```shell
$ uv publish
```

### Cloning on Another Machine

When another team member clones the project:

```shell
$ git clone <uri>
$ cd mypackage
$ uv run mypackage
Hello from mypackage!
$ uv run mypy
```

_(Note that `uv run mypy` works out-of-the-box because `mypy` is a dev-dependency and `uv run` or `uv sync` defaults to install all dev deps. The published package won't have `mypy`)_

**`uv` automatically handles the environment, resolving dependencies and running the entry point without manual setup!**

## `uv` CLI

The `uv` CLI provides the following commands:

- [`uv run`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-run): Run a command or script
- [`uv init`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-init): Create a new project
- [`uv add`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-add): Add dependencies to the project
- [`uv remove`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-remove): Remove dependencies from the project
- [`uv sync`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-sync): Update the project’s environment
- [`uv lock`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-lock): Update the project’s lockfile
- [`uv export`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-export): Export the project’s lockfile to an alternate format (like `requirements.txt`)
- [`uv tree`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-tree): Display the project’s dependency tree
- [`uv tool`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-tool): Run and install commands provided by Python packages (like `pipx` or `npx`)
- [`uv python`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-python): Manage Python versions and installations
- [`uv pip`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-pip): Manage Python packages with a pip-compatible interface
- [`uv venv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-venv): Create a virtual environment
- [`uv build`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-build): Build Python packages into source distributions and wheels
- [`uv publish`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-publish): Upload distributions to an index
- [`uv cache`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-cache): Manage uv’s cache
- [`uv self`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-self): Manage the uv executable
- [`uv version`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-version): Display uv’s version
- [`uv help`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-help): Display documentation for a command

comments.body: Also just dropping by to +1 this feature. uv seems to be more agnostic than conda. With uv, you can simply abstract the dependencies of your project not only at lightning speed, but also in a manager-agnostic way via `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, and even the `uv.lock` file, which ensures environment reproducibility and dependency tracking. It would be a huge upgrade to replace the current conda implementation with uv (given more and more developers are adopting it, seems to be a future-proof decision MLflow should definitely adopt).

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
## Design Document: UV Package Manager Support

I've drafted a detailed design document for implementing UV support in MLflow:

**Design Doc:** https://github.com/participant16/design-docs/blob/main/mlflow/mlflow-uv-support-design-doc-v1.md

### Summary

**Phase 1 (MVP):** Automatic UV detection and dependency export
- Detect `uv.lock` in project directory during `log_model()`
- Export to pip-compatible `requirements.txt` via `uv export`
- Graceful fallback to existing pip inference
- 100% backwards compatible - no API changes required

**Key Features:**
- Monorepo support (walks up parent directories)
- UV version checking (requires 0.5.0+)
- Observability tags (`mlflow.requirements.source`)
- Comprehensive error handling with fallbacks

**Phase 2 (Future):**
- Store `uv.lock` alongside model artifacts
- Add `env_manager="uv"` for faster environment restoration
- UV workspace support

### Requesting Feedback

@participant1 Would appreciate your architectural review of this approach. Happy to address any concerns or iterate on the design.

The design prioritizes backwards compatibility and "just works" behavior for UV users while maintaining all existing pip functionality.

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
**Update: Implementation Ready for Testing (PR #20344)**

I've implemented native UV support for MLflow's automatic dependency inference. The PR is ready for community testing and feedback.

**What's implemented:**

- Automatic UV project detection (`uv.lock` + `pyproject.toml` in CWD)
- Dependency export via `uv export` -> `requirements.txt`
- UV artifacts logged with model (`uv.lock`, `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version`)
- Monorepo support via explicit `uv_lock` parameter
- Dependency groups support (`MLFLOW_UV_GROUPS`, `MLFLOW_UV_ONLY_GROUPS`, `MLFLOW_UV_EXTRAS`)
- UV-based environment restoration functions

**Basic usage (just works):**
```python
# If you have uv.lock + pyproject.toml in your project directory
mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, "model")  # UV detected automatically
```

**Monorepo support:**
```python
mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, "model", uv_lock="/path/to/monorepo/uv.lock")
```

**Configuration:**
```bash
MLFLOW_LOG_UV_FILES=false python train.py  # Disable UV file logging
MLFLOW_UV_ONLY_GROUPS="serving" python train.py  # Export only serving deps
```

**To test:**
```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/20344/head
```

PR: #20344
Design doc: https://github.com/participant16/design-docs/blob/main/mlflow/uv-support-design-doc-v2.md

Would appreciate feedback on the API design and any edge cases I should handle.

Thankyou @participant19 and @participant4  for reviewing design and providing valuable feedback!

This shipped in **MLflow 3.11.1**. MLflow now supports `uv` for model dependency management: when you log a model from a uv project it detects `uv.lock` / `pyproject.toml` and can restore the environment with uv. Docs: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/model/dependencies
